Speed and agility are the problem: it is too slow to get away from most modern fighters and too sluggish to evade their missiles.
ba_65_a80: A single-seat variant of the Ba.65 light attack monoplane, the A.80 got its Fiat engine from airframe 82 onwards in 1938 because the original Isotta Fraschini K-14 was too weak; it was obsolete by 1940 but rushed to North Africa, where most were lost by early 1942. Added in Update 2.55 "Ninth Wave", its main change from the tree version is that engine, which brings a noticeable power gain and slightly better flight performance. It loses the rear gunner, though, and otherwise remains a light attacker with decent payload and guns but mediocre handling and low survivability.
ba_65_k14_l: Breda's Ba.65 (K.14) L, an Italian ground attacker, arrived in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica". Spawning in the air in Realistic battles offsets a low top speed, and plenty of ammunition plus strong forward guns for its rank make head-on passes worth taking. The 7.7 mm tail gun is effective at close range with Universal belts, flaps can slow it during strafing runs to put more rounds on target, and four 50 kg bombs are the best choice against the light vehicles it meets.
bb-1: Commissioned by Stalin as a multirole reconnaissance attacker under the code name "Ivanov", the ANT-51 was designed by P.O. Sukhoi at Tupolev's bureau and flew in 1937; underpowered at first, it entered production as the BB-1 short-range bomber once fitted with the M-87 engine. In the game since the open beta, it is a forgiving introduction to attackers, slow but happy to hug terrain and loiter over the battlefield, bombing and strafing trucks, AA guns and light tanks. A fast-firing rear ShKAS deters pursuers, and large wings give it a surprisingly tight turn when forced to fight.
be_6: Beriev's Be-6 was a long-range Soviet flying boat for anti-submarine, transport and reconnaissance work, first flown in 1949 with ASh-73 engines and a range above 4,000 km, and serving until the late 1960s. A premium pack since Update 1.71 "New E.R.A.", it was withdrawn from sale following 2018's Victory Day offers and came back for Golden Eagles at the 6th anniversary. Five NR-23 cannons in nose and tail turrets make it one of the best-defended bombers in the game, and its full payload can destroy two bases in Air RB.
beaufighter_mk1_40mm: To trial new 40 mm guns in summer 1941, a Beaufighter Mk I from the pre-production batch lost its 20 mm cannons, external stores and defensive guns in favour of the Rolls-Royce BH and Vickers S designs, and the Vickers won further development. A Battle Pass Season V ("River Hunter") reward, it carries no bombs or rockets, but its 40 mm cannons penetrate the thinner armour of tanks and blow apart large fighters and bombers. With only those big guns, small agile fighters are hard to hit.
beaufighter_mk21: Built in Australia by the government's Department of Aircraft Production, the Mk 21 Beaufighter dates from the game's open beta. It flies much like the Mk X but with stronger weapons: rockets and cannons make it excellent against convoys, and 12.7 mm guns replacing the Mk X's rifle-calibre weapons help when hunting bombers. The extra weight makes it slow, sluggish in turns and poor at climbing, so stay at medium or low altitude, avoid torpedo runs with their awkward drop limits, and seek fighter cover against nimbler enemies.
beaufighter_mk6c: The Beaufighter Mk VIc, in the game since the open beta, is one of the best heavy fighters at the low ranks: fully upgraded, its four 20 mm Hispano cannons tear down bombers and fighters alike. It handles best around 500 km/h, as controls become heavy at higher speed, so it suits head-on and tail-chase attacks more than boom-and-zoom; use the high spawn to set up attacks. If a single-engine fighter catches it, dive and climb away, or rely on the quick-firing turret, which can snipe pilots, or on turning.
beaufighter_mkx: The Mk X was the Coastal Command version of Bristol's Beaufighter, a heavy fighter that borrowed parts from the Beaufort; Hercules XVII engines improved low-altitude performance, and 2,231 were built from 1942 to 1945 with .303 guns, rockets and heavier bombs. In the game since the open beta, it keeps the Mk VIc's strong gun armament for air combat, which is of little use against ships and armour, but its bigger rocket and bomb loads can destroy even heavy tanks. The extra weight leaves it noticeably slower and less agile than the Mk VIc.
beaufort_mkviii: The Beaufort Mk VIII has been in the game since the open beta and wears Australian markings despite sitting in the British tree. Fast and nimble for a bomber, it excels at low-level attacks, where four 250 lb or two 500 lb bombs can wreck tanks, heavy ones included, and twin rear .50 cals give strong defence for its rank. Dive gently towards the target after spawning, without overspeeding as the controls lock up, and stay low because the turret cannot cover below; afterwards, rearm or hunt fighters with the tail gunner.
bf-109a_1: This premium Bf 109 A, added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", wears the colours of Norbert Flegel of the Condor Legion in the Spanish Civil War; it was also a free gift in 2017's German Unity Day event. It holds its own against similar aircraft but is short on power, handling and firepower, so conserve energy and use boom-and-zoom attacks on larger targets. Its two 7.92 mm MG 17s struggle against heavy aircraft, and much of its appeal lies in the two-blade wooden propeller and distinctive camouflage, making it more a collector's piece.
bf-109b_2: The Bf 109 B, rather than the A, was the first production 109, winning an early-1930s contest to replace the He 51; a planned hub cannon was dropped over cooling problems, and the Jumo 210D gave the B-1 only about 467 km/h, far behind the Merlin-powered Hurricane. Added in Update 1.49 "Weapons of Victory", it is underpowered at around 650 hp, climbs slowly at 10.2 m/s and has no cannon. Biplanes easily out-turn it, so gain height by side-climbing and use the high 790 km/h structural limit for boom-and-zoom passes, aiming for the pilot since two 7.92 mm guns do little damage.
bf-109c_1: The Bf 109 C-1 answered criticism of the B model with two extra wing-root machine guns and a fuel-injected Jumo 210G that kept running under negative g; just 58 were produced in 1938, and 20 went to fight in Spain's civil war, before the cannon-armed C-2 followed. Added in Update "Alpha Strike", it is a weak early monoplane with an underpowered engine that cannot turn with biplanes, and its four 7.92 mm guns struggle against bombers. In return it is fast and reasonably durable.
bf-109c_1_promo: Earned through War Thunder Mobile missions during Update "Dance of Dragons", this C-1 is otherwise a standard early 109. Historically the C-1 answered complaints about the B model with wing-root machine guns and a fuel-injected Jumo 210G; just 58 were built in 1938, with 20 sent to Spain. In play it is quick and fairly tough but underpowered, hopeless at turning with biplanes, and its four rifle-calibre guns make bombers a struggle.
bf-109e-1: The Emil answered the ageing early 109s in 1939 with the DB 601A engine, a three-blade variable-pitch propeller, reworked wings with better cooling and more nose-gun ammunition, though it still lacked self-sealing and drop tanks. Added in Update 1.35, the E-1 is lightly armed with just four rifle-calibre guns. Its flight performance is middling for a monoplane, but a decent engine and low weight make it a solid all-rounder against other early monoplanes, and a fuselage bomb rack lets it take on ground targets as well.
bf-109e-3: The Bf 109 E-3, in the game since the open beta, is essentially the E-1 with a real punch: a pair of 20 mm MG FF cannons in the wings means brief bursts are enough to bring enemies down, though these older guns cannot fire the potent Minengeschoss shells of the later MG FF/M. It is a fine energy fighter against its contemporaries but often meets late-war types like the P-47D, so engage those only with an energy advantage and drag attackers down to bleed their speed. Its reputation as a poor turner comes from comparisons with the Spitfire; with combat flaps it out-turns many better-armed opponents.
bf-109e-3_japan: Japan bought five Bf 109 E-7s in 1941 for evaluation; the Army judged them inferior to its new Ki-44, unaware that the F model was already in German service, and the main legacy was a licence for the DB 601 engine. Present since the open beta under the "E-3" name, it took the E-7 designation with Update 1.65 "Way of the Samurai". Two MG FF/M cannons with 60 Minengeschoss rounds each give a devastating burst, and it outclimbs and outruns most contemporaries. Against faster types like the P-47D-25, fight only with an energy edge, and treat turning, heavier than in the E-3, as a last resort.
bf-109e-4: A little heavier than the E-3, the E-4 (added in Update 1.53 "Firestorm") is nonetheless faster thanks to a smoother surface finish and 150 extra horsepower on WEP, and above all its MG FF/M cannons fire thin-walled Minengeschoss HE shells, 60 per gun. It flies like the other Emils: a strong energy fighter against its peers, but often matched against later aircraft like the P-47D, which should only be engaged from above. Combat flaps make it a respectable turner, though the extra weight means flat turns are a last resort.
bf-109e-7: The E-7 was a development of the E-4 with a new aerodynamic spinner and extra racks that also took drop tanks for range. This E-7/U2 arrived in Update 1.53 "Firestorm" as a 2015 Thunder League reward, later appeared in Warbonds trophy chests in April 2018, and is now obtainable only on the Marketplace. In play it is an Emil with MG FF/M cannons firing Minengeschoss shells, an energy fighter that must avoid P-47D-25s and similar types unless it has height in hand. With flaps it turns respectably, but the heavier frame makes sustained flat turns a bad idea.
bf-109f-1: The F-1 laid the groundwork for the Friedrich series, refining the 109's aerodynamics, especially around the nose, and fitting a DB 601 N of up to 1,175 hp. Added in Update 1.37, it reaches 615 km/h at 5.2 km and outclimbs most contemporaries, best at 270 km/h IAS, rewarding pilots who mastered energy tactics in the Emils. It trades the E-3's two wing cannons for a single nose-mounted MG FF/M with 60 mine shells, which is easier to aim but demands careful bursts at short range, backed by 1,000 rounds for the MG 17s.
bf-109f-2: The F-2 shared the F-1's refined airframe and 1,175 hp DB 601 N, with the same 615 km/h at 5.2 km and strong climb. Added in Update 1.37, it flies identically, but swaps the 20 mm MG FF/M for a 15 mm MG 151 with 200 rounds and better ballistics; hits come more easily, yet the lack of real HE means quick kills are rare and bombers need sustained bursts. Optional rockets can kill a bomber or tank in one hit but add drag. Its opponents dive and climb better but turn worse, so sustained turns can pay off and diving away rarely does.
bf-109f-4: Built after Spitfire Vs outclassed the Emil over the Channel, the F-4 brought the DB 601 E with over 25% more power and a hub-mounted MG 151/20 cannon free of synchronisation; over 1,800 were made, including reconnaissance versions, and it restored parity with the Spitfire. In the game since the open beta, it outclimbs many American fighters such as the P-51D-5 and P-47D-25, though they can keep pace because it is fairly draggy. The low-velocity cannon takes practice to lead, and the engine overheats under prolonged WEP, so manual engine control is advised.
bf-109f-4_hungary: Hungary licence-built the Bf 109 F-4, and one was flown by its top ace, Dezső Szentgyörgyi, in winter camouflage with the landing gear covers, radiator grille and tailwheel covers removed so snow could not clog them. It was a reward in Battle Pass Season X, "Royal Guard", for the Italian tree. Excellent handling, accurate and fairly powerful forward guns and a modest but useful bomb load make it a strong fighter. Its engine is fragile, and the missing fairings cost a barely noticeable amount of top speed compared with the German F-4.
bf-109f-4_trop: Present since the open beta, the tropicalised F-4 is a top-class energy fighter at its rank: plenty of power for its weight gives it a climb most rivals cannot match, ideal for diving attacks and luring pursuers into a losing climb. Keep WEP use in check or switch to manual engine control to avoid overheating, and expect the controls to lock up badly near 650 km/h. The optional 15 mm gondolas add little damage and cost agility, yet in vertical fighting, where turning matters less, the two extra MG 151s can decide whether a pass scores a kill.
bf-109f-4_usa: On 29 May 1942 two F-4s of 9./JG 3 got lost and force-landed in the USSR; one, works number 7640, went to the United States that November, was repainted olive drab as EB-1 (later EB-100) and impressed testers with its handling, engine and automation. In the game since the open beta, the American F-4 combines strong guns, an excellent climb and good all-round performance, making it a fine teacher of boom-and-zoom and energy tactics. It is fragile, especially its engine and cooling, the DB 601 needs temperature management to keep WEP available, and it has no external stores.
bf-109g-10: The G-10 bridged the Gustav and the Kurfürst by putting the DB 605D engine into a G-14-style airframe with a new cowling and bigger oil cooler, making it the fastest Gustav; it reached units in late 1944, and about 2,600 of a planned 6,000 were built. In the game since the open beta, it is very close to the G-14, with slightly better acceleration and top speed, a strong climb, responsive controls and heavy armament. The extra weight costs agility, so attacks need more planning.
bf-109g-14: The G-14 standardised improvements from earlier Gustavs, including the tall tail, a new engine and MW-50 water-methanol injection for much higher boost and speed than the G-6; more than 5,500 were built. Added in Update 1.47 "Big Guns", it pairs a hub MG 151/20 with 13 mm MG 131s, fewer rounds than the old 7.92s but far more damage with the right belt. A 30 mm MK 108 can replace the hub gun, though its poor ballistics limit it to point-blank range, and MK 108 or MG 151 gun pods are optional. Ground ordnance is limited to an incendiary bomb or a 250 kg bomb.
bf-109g-14as: As the Allies advanced through Italy in 1943, Italian units received Bf 109s from Germany, and after the September 1943 split, the RSI's air arm flew G-6s, G-10s and G-14s, including the G-14/AS with improved cooling. Added with the Italian tree in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", it is a strong energy fighter that turns poorly at low speed, so keep the speed up with boom-and-zoom passes and extend to set up the next attack. The AS modification makes it less prone to overheating than the German version, 30 mm or 20 mm cannons deal with any aircraft, and bombs help in mixed battles.
bf-109g-2: The G-2 replaced the F-4's DB 601 with the more powerful DB 605 in a similar airframe, and 1,586 were built in 1942; its extra weight disappointed some pilots, early engine and oil problems were acute in North Africa, and tropical versions gained a dust filter. In the game since the open beta, the G-2/trop is close to the F-4 with balanced handling and good guns, but two optional underwing 20 mm cannon pods reward diving energy attacks over drawn-out dogfights. Armour protecting the pilot and the rear tank makes it fairly durable for a fighter.
bf-109g-2_finland: Finland bought 30 Bf 109 G-2s in December 1942 to replace losses against Soviet fighters, eventually acquiring about 160 Gustavs, which greatly strengthened its air force and served until 1954. Added to the Swedish tree in Update 2.21 "Fire and Ice", it is similar to the F-4 in balanced handling and armament, but its stronger engine climbs better and reaches greater heights, an edge over its main rivals. Armour behind the pilot and around the rear tank adds survivability.
bf-109g-2_hungary: Hungary licence-built over 500 Bf 109s, mostly G series, keeping about half and sending the rest to Germany; they replaced CR.42 biplanes and fought with mixed success until the war's end. Added to the Italian tree in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy", the Hungarian G-2 handles much like the F-4 but climbs better and higher thanks to its stronger engine. Extra armour for the pilot and rear fuel tank improves survivability, though it is heavier overall and a little weaker at low altitude than the Friedrich.
bf-109g-2_romania: Romania received several hundred Gustavs and IAR built 49 G-2s locally as the Ga-2, the "a" meaning ausland; this one wears the colours of Ioan Dicezare of the 7th Fighter Group, credited with 16 confirmed kills plus three probables. Added to the German tree in Update 1.43, it is close to the F-4 with balanced handling and good guns, and optional underwing 20 mm cannon pods favour slashing energy attacks over long dogfights. Pilot and fuel tank armour make it reasonably tough, and it lacks the tropical filter of the G-2/trop.
bf-109g-6_erla_finland: The most produced Bf 109, the G-6 saw over 12,000 built between early 1943 and mid-1944, 13 mm MG 131s replacing the 7.92 mm guns and, on later aircraft, Erla's clearer three-piece canopy. Finland received 109 G-6s among 162 Gustavs from 1943 and used them until the war ended. Added to the Swedish tree in Update 2.21 "Fire and Ice", the Erla version handles and responds well at medium and high altitude and is fast and well armed, but it runs hot, so keep an eye on engine temperature.
bf-109g-6_finland: This premium Finnish G-6, added in Update "Red Skies", represents MT-422, one of 109 G-6s among the 159 Bf 109s Finland received for the Continuation War and one that served after the war; Sergeant Börje Hielm painted a shark mouth on it, which his commanding officer soon had removed. It performs exactly like the German tech-tree G-6, differing only in its Finnish paint and a tropical air filter, neither of which changes performance.
bf-109k-4: The K-4 Kurfürst, named after the Holy Roman Empire's prince-electors, was the final Bf 109, designed for easy production, yet no 109 accelerates harder or has more power for its weight, while the old airframe shows in poor high-speed handling. In the game since the open beta, it relies on climb rate, speed retention and boom-and-zoom attacks. Below about 450 km/h IAS it can out-turn the La-9, Typhoons, the P-47D and P-51s, but Spitfires and other late fighters are tougher; it is slow when stock and weak at low speed, and adding rudder in rolls speeds them up greatly.
bf-109z: Messerschmitt's Bf 109 Z-1 "Zwilling" joined two Bf 109 G-6 airframes into a single-seat heavy fighter to counter Allied bombers; the Z-0 prototype was bombed soon after completion, and the Z-1 was cancelled just before testing. A premium from Update 1.79 "Project X", it exceeds 700 km/h and is very hard to catch at altitude, but as a twin-engine fighter it should boom-and-zoom rather than dogfight. Four 30 mm MK 108s hit very hard but have such low velocity that long shots need heavy lead. It left the store after the 6th anniversary sale, returning briefly for later events.
bf-110c-4: The Bf 110 beat Henschel and Focke-Wulf for a 1930s heavy fighter requirement with better speed, range and firepower, succeeding as an escort over Poland and France before heavy losses in the Battle of Britain pushed it into night fighting and ground attack; the C-7 added two ETC 500 racks and uprated DB 601P engines. Present since the open beta as the C-4, it was reworked into the C-7 by Update 1.79 "Project X". Faster than most opponents, it concentrates two 20 mm cannons with 360 rounds alongside four MG 17s in the nose, a deadly package for high-speed boom-and-zoom passes.
bf-110c-6: The Bf 110 C, with DB 601A engines and clipped wings, was badly mauled by Spitfires and Hurricanes in the Battle of Britain; the C-6 was a small improvement on the C-4 with DB 601N engines and a 30 mm cannon. A rare premium reward from the Operation H.E.A.T event in Update 1.89 "Imperial Navy", it wears a unique scheme and carries four 7.92 mm guns plus one 30 mm cannon instead of the usual 20 mm pair, and a rear gun. With no external stores, the 30 mm must handle armour: HVAP rounds pierce as much as 77 mm but carry no explosive, so precise hits are needed.
bf-110g-2: When the Me 210 ran into serious design problems, the Bf 110 was updated instead, and the G series received DB 605B engines and aerodynamic refinements; the G-2, about 800 built between mid-1942 and April 1945, used Rüstsatz kits to act as interceptor, heavy fighter, bomber or attacker. Added in Update 1.79 "Project X", it is fast at altitude and heavily armed, making it a capable bomber interceptor, and its 37 mm cannon with excellent AP shells destroys ground targets. Weak rear defence and poor agility leave it exposed to single-engine fighters.
bf2c_1: Curtiss's BF2C Goshawk of 1933 developed the F11C with retractable landing gear and higher speed, but problems with that gear limited its US Navy career to a few months; it did better abroad as the Hawk III, mostly in China, Argentina and Thailand. Added in Update "La Royale", joining the P-26 Peashooters among US reserve aircraft, it is unusually fast for a reserve biplane because of its retracting undercarriage. It is agile like other biplanes but has only two .30 cal guns and small bombs, so keep height and use its speed to choose when to engage.
bf_109t_2: Built for the German carrier Graf Zeppelin, the Bf 109 T had larger wings, ailerons and flaps plus slats; only seven carrier-equipped T-1s were made, and the other 63 of the order became T-2s without naval gear, flying from short Norwegian mountain strips in 1941 and later with Jagdstaffel Helgoland and 11./JG 11 until 1944. Added in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force", it resembles the E-4 and E-7. Despite the bigger wing it is heavier, rolls worse and handles poorly at high speed, but otherwise turns and climbs well like early 109s; its armament is mediocre.
bf_110g_4: The G-4 was the Bf 110's dedicated night fighter, with DB 605B engines, larger tail surfaces, FuG 220 Lichtenstein radar and upward-firing Schräge Musik cannons that proved effective against bombers; 679 were built, or 2,208 counting sub-variants, from December 1942 to April 1945. Added in Update 2.1 "New Power", it intercepts bombers and attackers and strikes ground targets with speed, durability, strong guns and a large bomb load for its class. Unlike the G-2 it has radar for spotting high targets, which limits it to two gun pods instead of four, and it is far too clumsy to dogfight single-engine fighters.
bf_110g_4_hungary: The Bf 110 G-4 night fighter combined FuG 220 radar with a pair of upward-firing MG FF/M cannons, the Schräge Musik arrangement that let it attack bombers from below their guns; production began in summer 1942, and Hungary leased six. Added to the Italian tree in Update 1.101 "Raining Fire", it carries a varied arsenal of cannons, bombs of several sizes and large rockets, making it a good hunter of bombers and attackers as well as ground targets. Its poor agility means dogfights with fighters are best avoided.
bi: From 1940 Bolkhovitinov's bureau, with engineers Bereznyak and Isayev, developed the BI rocket interceptor; Grigory Bakhchivandzhi made its first powered flight on 15 May 1942, but corrosive nitric acid fuel quickly wore out airframes, he died when one dived into the ground, and jets made the idea redundant, though the rocket experience proved valuable. A 2020 "Strategist" wargame reward in Update "Raining Fire", it is rare and formidable when well flown, with instant acceleration and thrust nearly equal to its weight, but less than two minutes' fuel and scant ammunition. Diving is its weakness: the controls lock up beyond 600 km/h and become almost useless near 700 km/h.
blenheim_mkiv: The Blenheim Mk IV, in the game since the open beta, is a fast light bomber whose two 500 lb bombs are too little for attacking bases in Realistic, so it works best low and fast, releasing from very low height on smaller targets. Its only forward gun is mounted well outboard on the wing and takes practice to use. With flaps out it turns remarkably tightly at low speed, and its turrets can devastate inexperienced biplane pilots who sit close behind it, letting one Blenheim down many aircraft; tracer belts forward and universal belts in the turrets work best.
bo_105cb2: In 1985 a German BO 105 CB received TOW missiles and new optics as the CB-2 to compete in Sweden's anti-tank helicopter trials; it then returned home, and Sweden developed its own HKP9A. A premium pack from Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea", it has the family's superb agility for popping up from unexpected angles, firing its capable ATGMs (up to eight) and ducking back behind terrain. Countermeasures offer some protection from IR missiles and certain radar-guided SPAA, but without armour it is very vulnerable. Withdrawn following 2019's New Year offers, it returned for Golden Eagles in 2023 and 2024 flash sales.
bo_105pah1: The BO 105 PAH-1, an anti-tank derivative of MBB's BO 105M, could carry six HOT missiles; 212 reached the West German Army between 1979 and 1984, but its lack of night capability and poor survivability led to replacement by the Tiger, with the last retiring in 2016. Added in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea", it is small, quick and agile, ideal for fast strikes and quick withdrawals from ground fire, but has no armour at all. It carries HOT ATGMs plus heavy machine gun armament, and flares can be fitted against heat-seeking missiles.
bo_105pah1_a1: From 1991 part of the PAH-1 fleet was brought up to PAH-1A1 standard with HOT-2 missiles, better electronics and targeting, and new rotor blades, but limited night capability and survivability saw the Tiger replace them from 2007, with the army retiring its final BO 105s in 2016. Added in Update 1.83 "Masters of the Sea", it differs from the PAH-1 chiefly in firing HOT-2s with greater penetration. Otherwise it is the same small, fast, nimble helicopter for hit-and-run attacks, with no armour to protect it.
boomerang_mki: Fearing invasion and cut off from European suppliers, Australia built the CAC CA-12 Boomerang, its first indigenous fighter, loosely derived from the Wirraway trainer; it first flew on 29 May 1942, proved too slow to catch Japanese aircraft and moved to ground attack once P-40s arrived, with 105 built. In the game since the open beta, it out-turns almost everything it meets except most Japanese fighters. Its 20 mm cannons have little ammunition, so pick shots carefully, while plentiful .303 rounds suit light ground targets. It is slow for its rank and fights best at low altitude.
boomerang_mkii: The CA-13 Boomerang Mk II improved the CA-12's electrical systems and added provision for small bombs; 95 were built, and like the Mk I it could not catch Japanese bombers, so both moved to ground attack once P-40s became available in 1943. In the game since the open beta, its main difference from the Mk I is the ability to carry two 250 lb bombs. It turns better than nearly everything bar most Japanese fighters, but its cannon ammunition runs out quickly and its speed is low for its rank, so stay low, use the abundant .303 rounds on soft targets and pick cannon shots carefully.
boston_mk_1: The British Boston Mk I is a premium gift bomber present since the open beta, offered in 2014 to mark the A-20's first-flight anniversary, later found in September 2018 Warbonds trophy chests and now only on the Marketplace. It is very fast for its rank, often able to outrun its opponents in level flight. Four forward 7.7 mm guns give it some bite, and although the rear 7.7 mm guns look weak, armour-piercing or AP-incendiary belts aimed at a pursuer's engine can stop it, set it alight or hit the pilot.
br_20_dr: The B.R.20 was Italy's main bomber for much of the war, notably in North Africa, with 500 built between 1936 and 1943 and 82 sold to Japan, though it was criticised for unreliable engines and weak guns. Added with the first Italian aircraft in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", the B.R.20DR carries more bombs than most rivals and its gunners cover a wide area, though the dorsal gunner is often knocked out. Slow and sluggish, it may arrive too late in short Arcade and Realistic matches but is stable in Simulator. With turret guns aimed forward, three 7.7 mm guns and AP-I belts can surprise other bombers.
br_20m_m1: The most produced Cicogna, the B.R.20M M1 had a reshaped nose and 12.7 mm heavy machine guns in place of some 7.7 mm guns; the type was already outdated when war began yet served Italy until 1945, while Japan's examples were relegated to training in 1941. Added in Update 1.93 "Shark Attack", it is just as slow and sluggish as the earlier version but stable in Simulator, with a slightly larger bomb load than its peers and a more lethal 12.7 mm gunner. Poor performance and no armour make it an early target for interceptors, and its defence cannot cope with several fighters at once.
br_693_ab2: Bréguet's Bre 690 lost a 1934 three-seat bomber contest to the Potez 630 but was built anyway, impressing the air force on its first flight in March 1938; the Br 693AB2, with Gnome-Rhône 14M radials, reached 124 aircraft before the armistice and achieved little, later training crews for Vichy France and Germany. Since Update 1.93 "Shark Attack" it has offered a fairly agile twin-engine attacker with strong guns and an air spawn. Payload options are limited, the climb rate is mediocre and the defensive guns have awkward firing arcs.
breda_88: The Breda 88 was a mid-1930s heavy fighter whose prototype set several speed records and even raced, but once loaded with weapons and equipment it performed so poorly that it never served as intended. Added in Update 1.69 "Regia Aeronautica", it is fast in a straight line next to the surrounding biplanes but climbs badly, ruling out high-altitude fighting. Its three 12.7 mm Breda-SAFATs fire quickly and reach well, giving adequate punch, so stay on the edge of fights as a support fighter, picking off slow targets or helping teammates, since it is too heavy and clumsy to dogfight.
brigand_b1: Bristol developed the Brigand from its Buckingham as a Beaufighter successor for strike and torpedo work, but delays meant it arrived only in 1946, serving in training and in smaller wars, Malaya among them. Added in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters", it climbs and flies well enough to intercept bombers at altitude, where four 20 mm cannons in the nose make head-on attacks easy. Poor agility and roll rate make nimble targets a poor match, and once the bombers are gone, rockets and bombs let it help bleed the enemy's tickets through ground attack.
btd-1: The Navy ordered Douglas's XSB2D-1 in 1941 to replace both the Dauntless and the troubled Helldiver; it first flew in April 1943, and when the Navy asked for torpedo capability, the BTD-1 dropped the remote tail turret for more fuel and armour at some cost in performance, with just 26 built before Ed Heinemann asked for cancellation in favour of the Skyraider. Added in Update 1.33, it flies better than the SBD and SB2C, and carrying most ordnance internally keeps drag low. Bombs, torpedoes and mines suit ground and naval targets, airbrakes counter high-speed compression, and twin 20 mm cannons plus an air spawn make it a decent bomber hunter.
buccaneer_s1: The Buccaneer S.1 joined the Royal Navy in 1962 to fly low-level strikes, able to carry nuclear and conventional weapons, recognisable by its large nose and split-tail airbrake; powered by Gyron Junior turbojets, it flew from Ark Royal, Eagle and Hermes, including during the Aden Emergency and Beira Patrol, before the S.2 replaced it by 1970. A reward from the 2021 Summer Landing event during Update "Red Skies", it is one of few jet bombers with no guns, air-to-air missiles or countermeasures, so fighters, particularly those with radar and IR missiles, are a grave threat. Fly low and fast, hiding in terrain and cloud.
buccaneer_s2: The S.2 replaced the underpowered S.1's Gyron Juniors with stronger, more economical Rolls-Royce Spey turbofans, needing larger nacelles and reworked wings; all Navy Buccaneers were converted by 1966, the RAF adopted the type from 1969 after the TSR-2 and F-111K fell through, and it served until 1994. Added in Update "Hot Tracks", it outclasses the S.1 and Canberra B (I) Mk 6 with much more power, a 16,000 lb maximum bomb load, AIM-9Bs and countermeasure pods. It holds near-sonic speed even fully loaded, letting it hit one or two bases and run home with surprising agility, and AGM-12B Bullpups add a guided option.
buccaneer_s2b: After the Aden Emergency, the RAF needed a better anti-ship weapon and modified Buccaneer S.2s to guide the Anglo-French Martel missile by TV datalink; 49 S.2Bs were built from 1973 to 1977, but they saw little action, and in the Gulf War they mainly laser-designated targets for Tornados and Jaguars. Added in Update "Alpha Strike", it builds on the S.2 with internal countermeasures, all-aspect AIM-9Ls, a Pave Spike pod for Paveway bombs and the TV-guided Martel, whose long lock range and big warhead make it deadly against ground targets too. It remains large, heavy, clumsy and gunless.
bv-138c-1: The first aircraft from shipbuilder Blohm & Voss, the BV 138 "Seedrache" flying boat flew in 1937 and gained a third engine after stability and power problems, becoming the Luftwaffe's main maritime patrol aircraft; the C-1, with a four-blade propeller on the centre engine, was the most numerous version, 227 of 297 built. Added in Update 2.9 "Direct Hit", it is very slow and sluggish, so most aircraft catch it easily. Two 20 mm cannons and a 13 mm gun defend it well, and the hull absorbs plenty of rifle-calibre fire, but large blind spots above and below and poor agility leave it exposed to nimble attackers.
bv-155b-1: The BV 155 began as Messerschmitt's Me 155, a Bf 109-based carrier fighter, then became a high-altitude interceptor that Blohm & Voss redesigned with laminar-flow wings, bigger radiators and DB 603 engines; the V2 prototype survives at the National Air and Space Museum. A Battle Pass Season VIII ("Field Testing") reward from Update "Danger Zone", it performs best very high up thanks to its wing and supercharged DB 603. Getting there is slow at 13.8 m/s, the wing hurts roll rate, the 730 km/h structural limit is low, and most Air RB fights happen far below its ideal altitude.
bv-238: The largest Axis aircraft of the war, the BV 238 flying boat weighed as much as two B-29s and could fly over 10,000 km, but it only reached the prototype stage, the V1 being destroyed by the Allies while hidden near Lübeck. Added in Update 1.63 "Desert Hunters", it is slow but well armoured, can land on water, and its twenty 250 kg bombs can flatten a base. Twin 20 mm dorsal turrets and quad 13 mm mounts elsewhere make lone attacks from behind extremely risky; dive in fast from above at the pilots or engines instead, as losing a few engines brings it down slowly.
c_3604: Neutral Switzerland built the EKW C-36 ground attacker to replace Fokker C.V biplanes after bids for Bf 110s and Potez 63s failed; the C-3603 entered service in 1942 with a hub-mounted 20 mm Oerlikon, and the C-3604, of which 13 were built, added a stronger engine and two wing-mounted 20 mm Hispano cannons. Added in Update "Leviathans", it plays much like an IL-2: strong forward firepower, decent toughness and a surprisingly tight turn, with three cannons useful for air and ground work alike. Weak energy retention, top speed and climb and a modest rear gun are what opponents exploit.
ca_27_mk32_malaysia: Malaysia received 18 ex-RAAF CA-27 Sabres from 1969, flying them with the RMAF's 11th Squadron; five passed to Indonesia in 1976, and the rest were replaced by F-5s by 1978. Added to the Japanese tree in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey", no Sabre in the game weighs more, not even the F-86F-40 or CL-13 Mk.6, but its stronger engine keeps the power-to-weight ratio similar. It accelerates more slowly and, without slats, struggles in turning fights against many fighters. Strong cannon and missile armament and good energy retention still let it win longer engagements.
ca_27_mk32_raaf: Commonwealth Aircraft Corporation licence-built the F-86F but swapped the J47 for an Avon, requiring a reshaped fuselage, and added a pair of 30 mm ADENs; the final Mk.32 added the Avon Mk.26 and missile pylons, 69 were built, and RAAF Sabres served in the Malayan Emergency, the Konfrontasi and against insurgents in Laos, Thailand and Vietnam before Mirage IIIs replaced them by 1971. Added to the British tree in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey", the heaviest of the Sabres relies on extra thrust to balance the weight, but it accelerates slowly and lacks slats for dogfighting. Powerful cannons, missiles and good energy retention reward patient, extended fights.
canberra_bimk6: The B Mk 6 improved on the Canberra Mk 2 with stronger engines, wing fuel tanks and a slightly longer fuselage, and the interim B (I) Mk 6 interdictor added a ventral pack holding four 20 mm Hispanos, a pair of wing pylons and toss-bombing gear for nuclear weapons; it served from 1955, staying on nuclear alert until 1972. Added in Update 1.45 "Steel Generals", it is built for aggressive ground attack, keeping a bomb load while those four 500-round cannons make it a dangerous strafer and even a fighter. Nimbler than its size suggests, it can use its bomber spawn to ambush jet bombers or unwary fighters.
canberra_bmk2: English Electric, with former Westland designer W.E.W. Petter, answered a 1944 call for a Mosquito replacement with the Canberra; it flew in 1949, Korea prompted an order for 410, exports went to Australia and, as the licence-built B-57A, the US, and the first production B Mk 2s reached the RAF in 1951. Added in Update 1.43, it is an effective early jet bomber with a strong climb, decent speed and a bomber spawn, letting it climb away from interceptors or dive on bases. It has no guns at all, so survival depends on speed and its unexpected agility, and six 1,000 lb bombs can destroy a base.
caudron_cr714: A good bridge for pilots moving from biplanes to monoplanes, the C.R.714 arrived in Update 1.73 "Vive la France". Like most monoplanes other than light Japanese designs, it is heavier than a biplane and turns wider, though a stronger engine compensates. Originally conceived as a racer, it is at its best kept fast, and it bleeds speed quickly if drawn into a turning fight.
cf_188a_canada: Canada chose the F/A-18 Hornet in its New Fighter Aircraft programme to replace the CF-101, CF-104 and CF-116, the F-14 being too costly; twin engines, sturdy gear and good range suited Canadian needs, and 98 single-seat CF-188As plus 40 two-seaters were ordered in 1980, later seeing action in the Gulf War and NATO operations from the Balkans to Syria. Added to the British tree in Update 2.49 "Tusk Force", it is as effective as the American Hornet in both air and mixed modes, with AIM-7P and AIM-9L missiles, Paveways and two Maverick variants. It lacks a helmet-mounted display and active radar missiles.
cn_al_khalid_1: The Al-Khalid-I is Pakistan's upgrade of the Sino-Pakistani MBT2000 by Heavy Industries Taxila, adding fire-control and ergonomic improvements in the 2010s to keep pace with India's T-90S; officially introduced on 28 July 2020, it is replacing Pakistan's Type 59 and 69 tanks, with a Chinese engine and redesigned turret planned. Added in Update "Dance of Dragons", it handles, shoots and protects exactly like the MBT2000. A 1,200 hp engine and quick reverse make it well suited to flanking, and while its armour is not the best at its level, it occasionally saves the tank.
cn_antelope_tc_1l_ads: Taiwan's Antelope adapts the TC-1 air-to-air missile, developed for the F-CK-1 Ching-Kuo but left surplus once AIM-9s were plentiful, to a ground launcher on a Toyota Dyna truck; named after engineer Hsia Chieh-Ling, it was revealed in 1997, entered service in 2005 and serves with the Chaparral as Taiwan's last layer of air defence. Added in Update "Dance of Dragons", it works as a domestic Chaparral with a TV sight and radio rangefinder. Head-on locks reach only about 2.5 km, but the IRCCM-equipped TC-1L is deadly once it locks onto a jet from behind.
cn_cm11: To modernise its Pattons, Taiwan built the CM11 from M60A3 hulls, M48A5 turrets and an Abrams-class fire-control system, and it has served for more than three decades as a key part of the ROCA's armour, intended to counter landings; this version carries experimental GIAT explosive reactive armour from France. Added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it is slow and lightly protected against kinetic rounds, with distinctive pagoda-like ERA on the turret sides. Its 105 mm gun, shared with the M1 Abrams, a thermal sight and DM63 APFSDS let it do real damage when used carefully.
cn_cm_25: The CM25 is the Taiwanese marines' TOW carrier, part of the CM21 family that Taiwan reverse-engineered from the M113 after gaining experience rebuilding US Army M113s damaged in Vietnam. Added in Update "Raining Fire", it shares the M113's hull and drivetrain, but where the army's vehicles have polyurethane behind add-on armour plates, the marine version uses polystyrene for buoyancy. Its aluminium hull offers little protection and the extra weight makes it slower than an M113A1, so hide behind terrain or wrecks and fire I-TOW missiles or top-attack TOW-2Bs at approaching vehicles.
cn_cm_34: The CM34 is a 2014 IFV variant of Taiwan's CM32 family, developed from 2002 by the ORDC with Ireland's Timoney; it adds a 30 mm Bushmaster II cannon, ceramic composite armour and modern fire control, and was accepted in 2019 with at least 305 planned. Added in Update 2.51 "Spearhead", it is very versatile: the stabilised 30 mm, good optics and a laser warning system make it effective against both vehicles and aircraft. Only 90 rounds per belt and a 10-second reload may leave it unable to fire at key moments, and like other IFVs it is easily knocked out.
cn_fk_2000: CASIC's FK-2000 is an export air defence system first shown at Zhuhai in 2021, carrying radar, a dozen missiles and a pair of 30 mm cannons in a turret on an 8x8 truck to engage aircraft, cruise missiles and drones; buyers include Turkmenistan, Sudan, Ethiopia, Chad and the UAE. Added in Update 2.59 "Sky Odyssey", it closely resembles Russia's Pantsir, combining strong cannons with a phased-array radar and optical tracking. Its 12 missiles reach 26 km in ideal conditions, and the wheeled chassis lets it relocate quickly, but it is enormous and has no armour.
cn_gmc_cckw_353_m45_quad: Taiwan's army probably mounted M45 quad turrets on GMC CCKW 353 trucks, a workhorse since the war against Japan, as stand-ins for Taipei's 1961 parade marking the Republic's 50th year; they seem to have vanished once M35 trucks and SAMs arrived, leaving only parade photographs. Added in Update "Hot Tracks", it lacks the armour of the American M16 MGMC, but the M45 mount, with varied belts and easy ballistics, remains dangerous at low ranks. It fills a gap in the Chinese tree's early anti-aircraft line and carries plenty of ammunition.
cn_hj_9: The AFT09 carries the HJ-9, begun in 1988 to defeat modern tanks when the HJ-73 and early HJ-8 fell short; it switched from wire to TV guidance, used a tandem warhead and faster motors, and entered PLA service in 1999. Added in Update "Drone Age", it rides on the shortened WZ550 4x4 chassis of the WZ551 family, carrying up to twelve missiles and an unmanned retractable launcher with four ready to fire. Next to the similar French MEPHISTO it is more mobile going forward and its missiles beat the HOT-2 almost across the board, with penetration that kills even heavy tanks in one hit.
cn_hq_11: Developed to replace the outdated HQ-6, the system appeared as the export FM-3000 at Zhuhai in 2014, while the PLA's HQ11 version, adding a dedicated radar plus an LD-3000 gun vehicle for close defence, was only shown in 2022 and remains a prototype. Added in Update 2.53 "Line of Contact", it looks much like Israel's SPYDER, with a huge vehicle and extending radar mast. Powerful FM-3000 missiles guided by a phased-array radar handle aircraft at medium to long distances, but there is no optical guidance, so it depends entirely on radar.
cn_hq_17: Refused a licence for the Tor-M1 it had bought in the 1990s, China copied and upgraded it, revealing the HQ17 in 2015 with electronically scanned radars, a thermal sight and longer-ranged missiles; a wheeled version has been sold to Serbia and Saudi Arabia. Since Update "Storm Warning" it has served purely as an anti-aircraft vehicle: tall, protected only against rifle-calibre fire and full of electronics, so any penetration usually silences it. Its missiles outrange the Tor-M1's but their delayed motor ignition creates a large dead zone, and although the thermal sight tracks aircraft without tripping RWR, the bright smoke trail gives launches away.
cn_is_2_1943: Short of heavy tanks in the 1950s, China bought at least 38 IS-2s from the Soviet Union; at least 20 served in Korea against tanks and fortifications, before parts shortages and the Type 59 ended their service. The IS-2 (1943), added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", was the Chinese tree's first heavy tank. Its armour is fairly weak, but it moves well and its 122 mm D-25T fires an APHE shell with over 200 mm of penetration and enough explosive to knock out a whole crew. The reload is long, so use its reverse speed to back into cover between shots.
cn_is_2_1943_no402: IS-2 No.402 fought in Korea for the People's Volunteer Army at Ma Liangshan in November 1951, where terrain kept heavy artillery out and the tank served as an assault gun, destroying six British fortifications with HE shells; every crew member received a second-class merit medal. A premium released during the 2020 Lunar New Year sale in Update 1.95 "Northern Wind", it performs exactly like the IS-2, with a heavily armoured front and a big gun that kills any tank of its rank in one shot. Avoid angling, as the hull cheeks are much weaker.
cn_is_2_1944: The Soviet Union sold China IS-2s in the 1950s, and at least 20 fought in Korea before the cheaper Type 59 replaced them later that decade. The 1944 model, also from Update 1.91 "Night Vision", is the second Chinese heavy tank, gaining a far tougher upper glacis, comparable in effective thickness to a Tiger II, a commander's DShK and improved BR-471D ammunition that normalises well. Its 122 mm D-25T destroys almost anything it penetrates in one hit, but the long reload means retreating to cover between shots, and it moves well enough to reach early positions.
cn_isu_122: Where the ISU-152's howitzer was meant for fortifications and indirect fire, the ISU-122 mounted a 122 mm A-19 gun and hunted armour; China received 40 in September 1950, along with 300 T-34-85s and 60 IS-2s, as part of Soviet aid during the Korean War. Added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it is well armoured and shares its chassis and most characteristics with the ISU-152 and IS-2. Compared with the ISU-152 it penetrates more and reloads a little faster, and a roof-mounted DShK deters aircraft and light vehicles.
cn_isu_152: Nicknamed the "beast killer" for its answer to Tigers and Panthers, the ISU-152 was hard to aim from its casemate and often served as mobile artillery; when Soviet forces withdrew from Dalian in 1955, 67 were sold to the PLA, about 45 going to its new 1st Mechanized Division, and the type also supported troops in Korea. Added to the Chinese tree in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", it is well armoured and its 152 mm ML-20S howitzer threatens targets at any range. The reload is long, so fire only when confident of a hit; a roof DShK keeps aircraft and light vehicles at bay.
cn_lvt_4_zis_2: Nationalist and Communist forces both fielded amphibious LVTs in the Chinese Civil War, and the PLA seized many after 1949; when shells for the original 75 mm howitzer were no longer available, it rearmed them with a new turret carrying the high-velocity Soviet 57 mm ZiS-2, suited to fighting tanks and supporting infantry. Added in Update 1.91 "Night Vision", this American-Soviet hybrid is thinly armoured but dangerous at its rank, its gun reaching much further than the original version's. The open-topped turret and tall silhouette make it very vulnerable to aircraft and artillery.
